content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To measure jacket size, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Measure the distance from the shoulder seam to the wrist for sleeve length (2 minutes)
Step 2. Measure the circumference of the natural waistline (1 minute)
Step 3. Measure the width across the back from shoulder to shoulder (3 minutes)
Step 4. Record the final arm and shoulder dimensions on the size chart (5 minutes)
Step 5. Compare all recorded measurements against the manufacturer's size guide (10 minutes)
Step 6. Measure the circumference of the neck for collar sizing (1 minute)
Step 7. Double-check the chest and shoulder width for accuracy (2 minutes)
Step 8. Measure the torso length from the base of the neck to the hip (2 minutes)
Step 9. Identify the center point of the back for the starting measurement (30 seconds)
Step 10. Measure the widest part of the chest while breathing normally (2 minutes)
Step 11. Find a flexible tailor's measuring tape (5 minutes)
Step 12. Measure the bicep circumference with the arm relaxed (1 minute)
Step 13. Remove any bulky outer layers or sweaters (1 minute)
Step 14. Stand up straight with feet shoulder-width apart (30 seconds)
Step 15. Note the initial torso and back alignment (1 minute)
Step 16. Ensure the tape is level and flat against the back (45 seconds)
Step 17. Measure the distance from the nape of the neck to the waist (2 minutes)
Step 18. Wrap the tape around the fullest part of the shoulders (1 minute)
Step 19. Locate the top of the hip bone (30 seconds)
Step 20. Ask a friend to assist with reaching difficult areas (5 minutes)
Step 21. Put on a thin, well-fitting t-shirt for accurate base measurements (2 minutes)
Step 22. Note the arm and neck measurements in the notebook (2 minutes)
Step 23. Clear a space in front of a full-length mirror (5 minutes)
Step 24. Gather a notebook and a pen (3 minutes)
Step 25. Calculate the average of the torso and waist measurements (3 minutes)
Step 26. Check the wrist circumference for cuff sizing (1 minute)
Step 27. Read the instructions on how to measure for this specific brand (5 minutes)
Step 28. Position yourself in front of the mirror (1 minute)
Step 29. Calibrate the measuring tape against a ruler (2 minutes)
Step 30. Measure the over-arm circumference around the outside of the arms (2 minutes)

Question: Assume that you need to execute all the steps to complete the task and that infinite resources are available. What is the shortest possible time to measure jacket size?

The problem contains exactly 30 numbered steps. Your action ids must be:
step1, step2, step3, step4, step5, step6, step7, step8, step9, step10, step11, step12, step13, step14, step15, step16, step17, step18, step19, step20, step21, step22, step23, step24, step25, step26, step27, step28, step29, step30
